text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Dairies fear losing exports worth more than 100 million crowns if Denmark loses the right to call its feta style cheese by the name of feta, a name for which Greece is claiming exclusive rights. The dairies are therefore ready to fight for the right in a new European Union court case.

--- The closing down of the Swedish nuclear power station at Barseback, located within sight of Copenhagen, agreed by the Swedish government on Monday, is likely to result in higher electricity prices and more emissions from coal and oil-fired power stations, a Danish electricity industry official says.
--- The government is postponing important parts of its early retirement system reforms, expected to be introduced this spring.

--- From January 1, 1999, banks and mortage lenders will be able to offer loans in the European Union currency, the Euro, even though Denmark is not participating in the Economic and Monetary Union. The Euro loans will first of all be offered to export companies, with an interest rate 0.5 point lower than loans made in Danish crowns.
